about.title: A school of sound, a sanctuary of song
about.p1: Adullam Cave Choir was forged in seasons of quiet preparation — in the cave before the stage. We are a Ghana-rooted ministry training young voices, gifted instrumentalists, and worship leaders for excellence and reverence.
about.p2: From hands-on rehearsals to nationwide equipment installations, every note we shape and every speaker we hang is in service of authentic worship.

hero.title: Born in the cave. Built for the stage.
hero.subtitle: Our story is one of quiet preparation, raw devotion, and a calling that wouldn't let us go.

story.title: Our story
story.p1: Long before the lights and the live streams, there was a cave — a place of consecration where voices were forged, calluses formed, and a sound was born.
story.p2: What began as a handful of young singers in Accra has grown into a movement training choristers and equipping churches across Ghana and beyond.

vmv.title: Vision, Mission & Values
vmv.visionBody: To raise a prophetic generation of worshipers from the “caves” of life — people who have known distress, debt, and discontent, but are now commissioned as captains of sound. A choir that shifts atmospheres, heals nations, and prepares the way for the King, just as David’s men moved from the cave to the kingdom.
vmv.missionBody: To gather the distressed, the broken, and the overlooked into a company of worshipers, transforming pain into praise and misfits into minstrels for God’s glory. We exist to be a refuge where voices are restored and destinies are realigned through sound, presence, and community.

philosophy.title: Our training philosophy
philosophy.p1: The Cave is Not the End: We believe every cave season is a womb for greatness. Distress is raw material for depth. God recruits in caves and reveals in palaces
philosophy.p2: Sound Precedes Structure: Before David was king, he was a psalmist. We prioritize authentic worship over performance. Our sound is born from scars, not just skill.
philosophy.p3: Captain Over Us: Christ is our David — our Captain. We gather to Him, not to a platform. He transforms our complaints into chorus and our chaos into choreography.

equipment.title: We also equip churches
equipment.body: Beyond training, we install audio systems, configure stage rigs, and train worship teams to use them — because the right sound serves the right Spirit.

items.q1: How old do I need to be to apply?
items.a1: Our youngest program accepts students from age 8. Adults are welcome in our worship and instrument tracks.
items.q2: Do I need prior musical experience?
items.a2: For most programs, no. We start from the fundamentals. Some advanced tracks have prerequisites — listed on each card.
items.q3: Are programs in-person, online, or both?
items.a3: Most run in person in Accra. Selected modules are offered hybrid or online — see each program's format badge.
items.a4: Fees vary by program. We work hard to keep them accessible and offer scholarships in select cases.

steps.title: The application process
steps.s1Body: Complete the online form. It takes about five minutes.
steps.s2Body: Our team reviews every application personally.
steps.s3Body: Shortlisted applicants are invited for a short audition or interview.
steps.s4Body: Accepted choristers receive a welcome pack and orientation date.

items.i1: Open to applicants from age 8 upward (program-dependent).
items.i2: No formal music education required for most tracks.
items.i3: Applicants under 18 must have parental or guardian consent.
items.i4: A heart for worship and willingness to learn — non-negotiable.

items.a1: Usually two to three weeks from submission.
items.q2: Can I apply again if I'm not accepted?
items.a2: Yes — we encourage reapplication after a season of preparation.
items.a3: Limited scholarships are available based on need and gifting.
